title: Overshadowed by Ory; Roy Palmer's trombone
summary: He feels unrecognized next to Ory and says Roy Palmer shaded him in musicianship.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Like in the recent years, you haven't gotten very much recognition in Chicago.

Well, I've never. I feel this way. I've never got the recognition that I think I deserve. I've always been overshadowed by Ori. Yeah. You see what I'm talking about? You didn't have a band like that. Ori was a band.
Ori's been gone for years. Yeah, but. Ori was a band leader. That's the difference.

Yeah, Ori was a band leader. Ori is a. Orgin. Oh, and I, well, he wrote nice tunes, you know. And the tunes that he wrote. Of course he played with him a long time. And then this movie actor put his arms around him in California and he was broadcasting, I forget his name. Austin Wilson. Yeah, Austin Wilson. See, he was in this picture. This picture of Benny Goodman. And so I mean when a man was before the public, see I quit for six years. And I never has been as popular as Ori and I admit it. But I don't think he ever played any more trombone in me.
You think Roy Palmer played more trombone than you?

Well I think I'll give you an answer to that. I've been hearing Roy's records. I'll say this. Roy always could play better. Willie Humphrey said last night that George Field told him that Roy always was exact in playing trombone. No, I think Roy shaded me in musicianship for one thing, because Roy could read all the clefs. You see what I'm talking about? And I can. I'm just being truthful about it. But now I'm more aggressive than Roy was. It's a change of times. You see I had fellas tell me, I don't want you to play that way. I want you to play this way. I had some teeth pulled recently. And Franz told me, I'm going to tell you what he told me. He said don't play so whitish. I'm striving for tone. Tone you understand what I'm talking about? And he told me, don't play so you want me to play more like Higgy or somebody more rough. And I'm trying to play legato, I'm trying to play a hot solo with some legato, you understand? And he didn't want that. But to be truthful, there's no telling how much Roy could play because they accused him of being lazy. Now Roy would go to sleep. You see what I'm talking about? Roy, he just couldn't help that. I don't know what was wrong with it. And when that gets around, that hurts you. But the fellas, unfortunately the fellas from New Orleans, they didn't hire Roy much. They didn't hire much. Roy made his money with Cook and other bands. Yeah.
Well he had a funny attack sometimes. But then other times he could play very clean. His brakes were extremely clean. Yeah, yeah.
He had execution. Like Noah, all that, and like the higher society kind of part. He played all of that with his trombone.
But if he wanted to, he'd get a sort of a slap attack. When he wanted to, that's the thing. And it was funny. I thought he was funny at times.
Well that's the thing about Roy. Roy didn't have no one particular style. He had about two or three. It's according to the mood he was in. You see what I'm talking about?
He never did get much of a break in recording.
